speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any blood in your urine, and are you experiencing pain or burning when you urinate?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: BladderUltrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None; Pelvic Ultrasound: Postvoid Residual Urine 25 mL

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the urinalysis results showing no infection and normal ultrasound findings, the clear fluid and lack of bacteria rule out a standard urinary tract infection. Given your history of chronic discomfort and frequent urination, have you noticed any overflow leakage, difficulty starting your stream, or a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying? Additionally, do you experience pain or discomfort in your lower abdomen or pelvis?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The relief of discomfort after voiding and the presence of dyspareunia suggest irritation of the bladder trigone. Given your age and symptoms, have you noticed any difficulty starting your stream, a weak stream, or a sensation that the bladder is not completely empty? Additionally, have you experienced any vaginal dryness or pain during intercourse unrelated to infection?

REQUEST TEST: Postvoid residual measurement (recheck)

speaker: Doctor
text: The postvoid residual is normal at 25 mL, and your symptoms of urgency, frequency, and dyspareunia with relief after voiding are highly suggestive of Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. Given your age and lack of infection, have you noticed any clear, bloody, or "smoke-colored" urine, or is the urine always clear? Also, have you experienced any skin rashes, joint pain, or Raynaud's phenomenon (cold fingers/toes)?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS). The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency, urgency, dyspareunia, and negative infectious workup is classic for this condition.
